elements.evidence: 21.3 lists indemnification as an Excluded Claim; no 3× annual fees super-cap added

reasons: The document had no indemnity clause at all while Sections 9.3, 19.5 and 21.3 presuppose one; a single concise inserted Section 20 is a minimal cure for an absent clause.

All preferred atomic elements are present: Vendor defence and indemnity for Customer and Affiliates, the four triggers (IP infringement allegation, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incident, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), notice-control-cooperation procedure, and Customer's indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
No fallback-only material (exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, 3× super-cap) was imported, so the two bargains are not mixed.
Uses existing defined terms (Affiliates, Services, Deliverables, Customer Data, Applicable Law) and leaves 9.3, 19.5 and 21.3 fully effective; no contradiction or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Costs language ("including reasonable attorneys' fees") is ordinary scope of a defend-and-indemnify duty rather than added protection, and no hold-harmless, extra indemnitees or settlement mechanics were added.
